summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and recent PFO closure was admitted for evaluation of transient left facial droop noticed by her husband the prior evening. She denied symptoms and had no persistent deficits on exam, though initial testing showed subtle left-sided motor slowing. MRI revealed no acute infarct but showed linear enhancement in the left frontal operculum, concerning for either a small subacute stroke or metastatic involvement. Given her risk factors—including high cholesterol, recent PFO closure, and malignancy—a transient ischemic attack (TIA) was diagnosed. Her symptoms resolved completely during the hospital stay. Dual antiplatelet therapy was continued, but statin therapy was withheld due to advanced cancer. She was discharged home with stroke education, instructions to follow up with cardiology, and a rolling walker for support.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of left female breast
Secondary malignant neoplasm of unspecified site
